title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ector County, TX/NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ector County, TX | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Ector County minerals sit near the busiest oilfield hub in the Permian. See how a retired operations engineer prices royalty and working interests here.
heroLead: Odessa is the industry's front door to the Permian, and Ector County minerals underneath and around it get looked at differently than acreage further out.
intro: Ector County is where a lot of the Permian's service and supply chain physically lives, but underneath that infrastructure sits some genuinely productive Wolfcamp and Spraberry acreage, plus a long tail of older vertical production going back generations. I've bought interests in both categories here, and the valuation approach for each is different enough that I want to walk through it plainly.

If you own a royalty or working interest in Ector County, whether it came to you through inheritance or you've held it for years, the county's mix of urban proximity, dense drilling history, and layered ownership makes it worth getting a real look at your specific tract rather than a generic county-wide estimate.

sections.heading: Urban Odessa versus rural Ector County acreage
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Ector County's mineral estate sits under or near developed land around Odessa, which complicates drilling in ways that rural acreage in neighboring counties doesn't face. Setback requirements, surface use conflicts, and the practical difficulty of running a rig near residential or commercial development all factor into how operators plan around here.

Acreage further from the city, out toward Goldsmith and Gardendale, tends to see more straightforward horizontal development with fewer surface complications, and that generally shows up in how consistently those wells get drilled and produced. Neither situation makes an interest worthless, but it does change how I underwrite the risk.

sections.heading: Decades of layered production history
paragraphs: Ector County has been producing oil since the 1920s, and a lot of the current mineral ownership traces back through several generations of the same families. That long history means I regularly see interests tied to old vertical Permian-age wells still producing modest volumes alongside newer horizontal Wolfcamp units on the same or adjacent tracts.

When both exist, your royalty check might be blending income from multiple wells with very different decline profiles, which is exactly the kind of situation where a generic online calculator gets it wrong. I pull the actual well history tied to your interest before I put a number in front of you.

sections.heading: What actually sets the price
paragraphs: Net royalty acres, current production rate, decline stage, and nearby permitting activity are the core inputs, and they vary enough between a downtown-adjacent tract and a rural Ector County section that I won't quote a flat multiple for the whole county. What I can say honestly is that Ector County's dense operator activity and long production history tend to make title and production research more tractable than in newer, less-documented parts of the basin.

If your interest includes a working interest component rather than pure royalty, that changes the math meaningfully since you're on the hook for a share of operating costs. Tell me upfront which kind of interest you hold so the number I give you reflects your actual exposure.

sections.heading: Working with heirs and split ownership
paragraphs: Because Ector County minerals have passed through generations of the same families, it's common for an interest to be split among a dozen or more heirs, sometimes with some shares undivided and unclear. I can typically buy your specific share without requiring the rest of the family to participate, and I've walked plenty of owners through exactly what documentation is needed to clear title on an inherited fractional interest.

None of this is legal or tax advice, and for probate or estate questions specific to your situation, talk to your attorney or CPA. What I bring is a straight cash offer built on real production data and no pressure to sign before you're ready.

sections.heading: Timeline and what closing actually looks like
paragraphs: Once we agree on a number, I send a straightforward purchase and sale agreement, and my title work confirms your interest matches county and state records before anything closes. For most Ector County owners with clean title, that process runs three to six weeks from signature to funds in hand.

If there's an unresolved probate or a missing heir somewhere in the chain of title, that adds time, but it doesn't kill the deal. I've walked owners through exactly what curative steps are needed more than once, and I'm happy to explain what your specific situation requires before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: Does it matter if my Ector County interest is near Odessa itself?
faqs.answer: It can. Acreage close to developed parts of the city faces more surface-use and setback constraints on new drilling, which factors into value differently than open rural acreage further from town.

faqs.question: My check comes from an old vertical well, is that interest still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes, especially if there's newer horizontal development nearby or on the same tract. Even a modest, long-declining vertical well interest has value, and I evaluate it against actual production data rather than dismissing it.

faqs.question: I share ownership with several cousins I've never met, can you still buy my portion?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can typically purchase your specific fractional share independently. I'll ask for documentation showing how you hold title, but the rest of the family doesn't need to be involved for your sale to close.

faqs.question: How do you value a mix of working interest and royalty in the same Ector County unit?
faqs.answer: I price each component separately, since working interest carries cost exposure that royalty doesn't. Send me your division order or JIB statement and I'll break down what each piece is realistically worth.
